rics.meaning: Government External Debt — central + local-government foreign-currency debt + non-resident-held CGBs (Chinese Government Bonds). Largest component is foreign holdings of onshore RMB CGBs.
rics.how_to_use: Foreign CGB holdings indicator. Bond Connect and CIBM Direct allow foreign investors to hold onshore CGBs; foreign holdings ~5% of total CGBs outstanding. Sharp inflows/outflows correlate with USD-CNY moves.

rics.description: Total External Debt, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Total External Debt, YoY change — pace of external-debt accumulation.
rics.how_to_use: Track for external-vulnerability buildup. China's external debt growth slowed sharply post-2022 with USD strength + capital-control tightening. Watch alongside FDI for net foreign claims direction.

rics.meaning: Total External Debt — debt owed to non-residents (FX + RMB-denominated debt held by foreigners). ~$2.5 trillion (2024). Published quarterly by SAFE.
rics.how_to_use: China external debt is moderate at ~14% of GDP (vs 30% for India, 50%+ for many EM peers). Composition: ~60% short-term (mostly trade credits + interbank), ~40% long-term (sovereign + corporate bonds). Foreign holdings of CGBs are ~$200 billion.
